<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

port Python's HF-renderer fallback for templates without a `developer` role (#43590), so developer instructions are no longer silently dropped or rejected by templates such as Qwen3 and Qwen3.5.

review order: [1/3: renderer #63901](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63901) → [2/3: non-streaming #63902](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63902) → [3/3: streaming #63903](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63903). all three upstream review PRs target `main`; later diffs include earlier layers.

## Claims

- like Python, when a request has developer messages and the template text lacks `"developer"`/`'developer'`, rename them to `system` (dropping message-local tools) and merge all system messages into the first one.
- preserve string and OpenAI-array content shapes when merging. a merge that would move a non-leading system/developer message with media ahead of earlier media returns a 400 instead of reordering media: templates can reorder messages arbitrarily, so placeholder order cannot be predicted in general, and Python fails on the same input after flattening the content to text.
- keep the change in the shared Chat Completions/Responses renderer; this layer adds no endpoint.

## Validation

### October 30 — `9afc738e37` (BugenZhao)

stacked `9afc738e37` on `90cc52cdd0`: replaces the media reordering (`renderer/hf/media.rs`, `media_order`) with the 400 above.

- `cargo fmt --check`, strict Clippy for chat/server/text, and `cargo nextest run -p vllm-chat -p vllm-server -p vllm-text`: **1142 passed** on this head, **1170 passed** with this head merged into `main` `24420b7a34` (includes #63963 and #64274).
- parity with Python: rendered the cached Qwen3-0.6B, Qwen3.5-0.8B, Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B, and Gemma 4 E2B templates through the Rust renderer and through `vllm/renderers/hf.py`'s conversion functions with Jinja2, for developer first, after system, mid-conversation, alongside a mid-conversation system, and a no-developer control. on the three Qwen templates, which take the fallback, every string-content prompt matches byte for byte. two pre-existing differences also appear without developer messages and are outside this PR: Rust joins text parts without `\n` under the string format (#63974), and Gemma 4, which supports `developer` and so never takes the fallback, renders a trailing space after system content.

### Latest upstream synchronization — October 28

current head: `90cc52cdd0`; rebased onto upstream `f4fd1ab68e`. the fork keeps its native stacked bases; upstream PRs still target `main`.

- resolved the shared error-handler overlap with upstream's missing-LoRA 404 change. both `NotFound` and `ResponseNotFound` retain their existing wire envelopes; the LoRA/gRPC and Responses HTTP regressions pass.
- `cargo test --locked -p vllm-chat --lib -- --test-threads=1`: **438 passed** as part of the full-stack run.
- strict Clippy for server/chat/text/CLI, applicable pre-commit hooks, and `git diff --check`: passed. `cargo nextest` remains unavailable.
- range-diff shows only the error-handler conflict adaptation; all other feature/fix patches are unchanged. all branch tips passed merge-tree checks against `f4fd1ab68e`.
- the old umbrella #58783 was synchronized without rewriting its original history. its source tree equals the tested complete stack and it stays draft.

the model-backed HTTP/Codex evidence below predates this synchronization (complete-stack head `3db4c9abf0`); it was **not repeated after this rebase**. today's evidence covers compilation and deterministic wire/route/renderer regressions, not new model qualification. CI reruns on these new heads are separate from the earlier successful workflows. agentic-api was not changed or pushed.

### Earlier review and runtime evidence

reviewed again on October 27; renderer head: `699ef82150`. no new renderer change was needed.

- `cargo test --locked -p vllm-chat --lib -- --test-threads=1`: **430 passed**.
- the final stack's full server/chat/text suite passed **1,107 tests** (one existing text test ignored).
- strict Clippy, applicable pre-commit hooks, formatting, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- all three tips merge cleanly with upstream `f8f7634cb4` using `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main <layer>`. the fork's isolated stack bases are preserved.

commands ran from `rust/` with `OPENSSL_DIR` pointing to the local OpenSSL build. `cargo nextest` was unavailable. tests ran serially after the previous parallel chat run exposed a shared audio-metrics collector collision; the isolated test and complete serial suites passed.

fresh model-backed HTTP and real Codex checks on the revised **complete stack** are recorded in #63903. these are text/function-tool interoperability checks, not a multimodal evaluation. deterministic renderer/media-extraction regressions cover string and OpenAI-array content formats; fresh model-backed multimodal qualification remains outstanding.

## Details

a plain-string merge can lose policies for array-based templates, so the merge preserves the effective content representation. moving system/developer messages can also reorder placeholders without moving their media; such requests are rejected rather than reordered.

the rebase retains upstream's request-template fuel controls and uses the normal template constructor in the new upstream fuel-test fixture. the renderer changes also affect Chat Completions.

these are the existing #58783 layers opened upstream at [@BugenZhao's request](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58783#issuecomment-6418403089), rather than competing implementations. the original authored history and discussion remain in #58783. @gcanlin's #53380 implementation is credited in the endpoint and streaming commits. duplicate checks found #63497 affects DeepSeek renderers and #56391 affects Python's HF renderer; neither covers this Rust HF path. the [fork layer](https://github.com/franciscojavierarceo/vllm/pull/1) retains the isolated review history.

diff against the new base: **3 files, +212 / -9**. Codex assistance was used. human review of every changed line and independent validation remain required before merge.

- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>
